title: SpaceX tells NASA it will retire Crew Dragon after 2030, halting low-Earth orbit human spaceflight
summary: SpaceX has informed NASA that it will no longer fly Crew Dragon missions to low-Earth orbit after 2030, effectively ending the company's role in NASA's commercial space station economy. The decision threatens plans for private space stations and represents a significant shift in NASA's two-decade st
takeaways: SpaceX agreed to support the International Space Station until 2030, then plans to retire Crew Dragon
SpaceX has declined orders from private space station companies (Axiom Space, Voyager Space, Vast Space) for Crew Dragon missions

title: NASA Administrator Issues Directive to Loosen Planetary Protection Rules for Mars Missions
summary: NASA administrator Jared Isaacman has issued a directive easing decades-old "planetary protection" regulations designed to prevent Earth microbes from contaminating Mars and other worlds. The policy shift argues that sterilization standards established in 1969 no longer reflect current scientific kn
takeaways: The 1969 rules required less than a one-in-10,000 chance of exposing Mars to Earth-origin microbial life; the new directive seeks to modernize these standards
NASA administrator Jared Isaacman cited improved sterilization technology and the need to lower mission costs and increase commercial capabilities
The policy shift was announced via an internal NASA message obtained by watchdog sites NASA Watch and Astrobiology.com
Original planetary protection rules were established in 1964 by the International Council for Science's Committee on Space Research (COSPAR) amid Cold War space race concerns
